_note: English source texts for the starter stories. scripts/stories/generate.php turns each one into all 11 languages (data/stories/<slug>.json). One array item per sentence: every translation keeps the same sentences in the same order, so a word's example sentence can be shown in the learner's own language. Religious stories follow well-attested narrations (see 'source'); popular stories without a reliable chain are left out.

stories.source: German legend, as told by the Brothers Grimm (public domain)
stories.title: The Pied Piper of Hamelin
stories.summary: A stranger rids Hamelin of its rats with his pipe, and the town breaks its promise.
sentences: The town of Hamelin was full of rats.
They ran through the houses, ate the bread and bit the dogs.
One day a stranger in a coat of many colours came to the town hall.
"I can take all the rats away," he said, "if you pay me a thousand coins."
The mayor agreed at once.
The stranger took out a small pipe and began to play.
From every house the rats came running and followed him.
He walked into the river, and all the rats went in after him and drowned.
But when he asked for his money, the mayor only laughed.
"The rats are gone," he said. "Why should we pay you now?"
The piper said nothing and left.
A few weeks later he came back and played a new, sweet tune.
This time the children came out of the houses and followed him.
He led them up to a mountain, and a door in the rock opened and closed behind them.
Only one boy, who could not walk fast, stayed behind.
The people of Hamelin learned too late that a promise must be kept.

stories.title: The Little Match Girl
stories.summary: On New Year's Eve, a poor girl lights her matches one by one to keep warm.
sentences: It was very cold on the last evening of the year.
A poor little girl walked through the snowy streets with bare feet.
In her old apron she carried matches, but nobody bought any.
She was afraid to go home, because her father would be angry.
She sat down in a corner between two houses.
Her hands were almost frozen, so she lit one match.
In its warm light she saw a big iron stove.
But the match went out, and the stove was gone.
She lit another match and saw a table with a roast goose.
With the third match she saw a beautiful Christmas tree full of candles.
Then she lit one more and saw her dear grandmother.
"Grandmother, please take me with you!" she cried.
She quickly lit all the matches so her grandmother would not disappear.
Her grandmother took her in her arms, and they flew up to where there is no cold and no hunger.
In the morning people found the little girl in the corner.
She was smiling, but nobody knew what beautiful things she had seen.

stories.title: Chicken Little
stories.summary: An acorn falls on Chicken Little's head, and she is sure the sky is falling.
sentences: One day an acorn fell on Chicken Little's head.
"Oh no! The sky is falling!" she cried.
"I must go and tell the king."
On the way she met Henny Penny, Ducky Lucky and Goosey Loosey.
"The sky is falling!" she told them, and they all ran with her.
Then they met Foxy Loxy.
"I know a short way to the king," said the fox with a smile.
He led them straight into his dark den.
Only Chicken Little was quick enough to run away.
And the sky? It never fell at all.

stories.title: Snow White
stories.summary: A jealous queen, seven dwarfs and a poisoned apple.
sentences: Once upon a time there was a princess called Snow White.
Her skin was as white as snow and her hair was as black as ebony.
Her stepmother, the queen, had a magic mirror.
"Mirror, mirror on the wall, who is the fairest of them all?" she asked every day.
One day the mirror answered: "Snow White is the fairest of all."
The queen was so jealous that she sent Snow White into the forest.
Snow White ran until she found a little house.
Seven dwarfs lived there, and they let her stay with them.
But the queen found out where she was.
She dressed as an old woman and gave Snow White a poisoned apple.
Snow White took one bite and fell down as if she were dead.
The dwarfs were very sad and put her in a glass coffin.
One day a prince came by and wanted to take the coffin with him.
When his servants lifted it, the piece of apple fell out of her mouth.
Snow White opened her eyes, and soon she and the prince were married.

stories.source: One Thousand and One Nights, 'The City of Brass' (public domain)
stories.title: The City of Brass
stories.summary: Travellers cross the desert to a city of brass, and find that its riches saved no one.
sentences: Long ago, the caliph in Damascus heard about old brass bottles hidden by the sea.
He sent the wise governor Musa ibn Nusayr to find them.
Musa and his men travelled through the desert for many months.
One day they saw a huge city with walls of shining brass.
There was no gate, so they had to climb over the walls.
Inside, the streets were silent.
The markets were full of silk, gold and jewels, but there were no people.
In the palace they found a queen on a throne.
She looked alive, but she had died long ago.
On a tablet beside her they read: "I had more gold than anyone.
But when hunger came to my city, gold could not buy one piece of bread."
Musa read the words and cried.
He took only what he had come for and left all the treasure behind.
On the way home he said to his men: "Riches do not last. Only good deeds do."

stories.title: The Prophet and the Camel
stories.summary: A camel cries when it sees the Prophet Muhammad, and he speaks to its owner.
sentences: One day the Prophet Muhammad, peace be upon him, walked into a garden in Medina.
A camel was standing there.
When the camel saw the Prophet, it made a sad sound and tears ran from its eyes.
The Prophet went to the camel and gently stroked its head.
Slowly the camel became calm.
"Who owns this camel?" the Prophet asked.
A young man came and said, "It is mine, O Messenger of Allah."
The Prophet said: "Do you not fear Allah about this animal that Allah has given you?
It has told me that you keep it hungry and make it work too hard."
From that day the young man took good care of his camel.

stories.title: The Woman and the Thirsty Dog
stories.summary: A woman uses her own shoe to give water to a dog dying of thirst.
sentences: On a very hot day, a woman was walking past a well.
She had done many wrong things in her life.
Beside the well she saw a dog.
It was walking round and round the well, almost dying of thirst.
The woman had no bucket and no rope.
So she took off her leather shoe and tied it to her headscarf.
She lowered the shoe into the well and filled it with water.
Then she gave the water to the dog until it was no longer thirsty.
The Prophet Muhammad, peace be upon him, told this story to his companions.
He said that Allah forgave the woman because of this one act of mercy.

stories.title: The Garden of Abu Talha
stories.summary: Abu Talha gives away the garden he loves most.
sentences: Abu Talha was one of the richest men in Medina.
He had many date gardens, but he loved one of them most of all.
It was called Bayruha, and it was close to the Prophet's mosque.
The Prophet, peace be upon him, often went there to drink its fresh, clear water.
Then a verse of the Quran came: "You will not reach true goodness until you give from what you love."
Abu Talha went to the Prophet and said: "The thing I love most is Bayruha.
I give it for the sake of Allah."
The Prophet was happy and said: "That is wealth that brings great profit!
I think you should give it to your relatives."
So Abu Talha shared the garden among his relatives and his cousins.

stories.source: Traditional story told about Ibrahim ibn Adham (8th century)
stories.title: The King of Balkh
stories.summary: A rich king hears a strange voice on his roof and changes his life.
sentences: It is told that Ibrahim ibn Adham was once the king of Balkh.
He lived in a great palace and slept on a soft bed.
One night he heard footsteps on the roof.
"Who is there?" he called.
"I am looking for my camel," answered a voice.
"You fool! How can a camel be on a roof?" said the king.
"And how can you find Allah on a soft bed in a palace?" the voice replied.
The king could not sleep for the rest of the night.
In the morning he put on a simple coat and left the palace.
He spent the rest of his life working with his hands, praying and helping the poor.

stories.title: The Sleepy Little Star
stories.summary: A little star is too tired to shine, and the moon helps her rest.
sentences: High in the night sky lived a little star called Lumi.
Every night she shone as brightly as she could.
But one night she felt very, very tired.
"I cannot shine tonight," she said quietly.
The big round moon smiled at her.
"Then rest, little one," said the moon. "I will shine for both of us."
Lumi closed her eyes and slept on a soft white cloud.
Down below, a boy looked up at the sky from his window.
"Good night, moon," he whispered. "Good night, little star."
And the next night, Lumi shone brighter than ever.

stories.title: The Bear Who Could Not Sleep
stories.summary: It is time for the winter sleep, but Little Bear is wide awake.
sentences: Winter was coming, and all the bears were going to sleep.
Little Bear lay in the warm cave, but his eyes were wide open.
"I am not sleepy," he said to his mother.
"Then let us count the things we saw this year," said Mother Bear.
"One: the river full of fish."
"Two: the tall tree with sweet honey," said Little Bear.
"Three: the yellow flowers on the hill."
"Four: the stars over the forest," said Little Bear, and he yawned.
"Five…" said Mother Bear softly.
But Little Bear was already asleep, and he dreamed of spring.
